toegepas.blok: Waar ons hulpbronne veral ontgin word
toegepas.rede_vinder: Standard Afrikaans says 'bekend om'; 'bekend vir' follows English 'known for'.
toegepas.fout: 'bekend vir' copies English 'known for'; Afrikaans says 'bekend om'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Fixes a direct translation from English without moving the meaning; protected names untouched.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Om' can be misread as 'because of'; 'rondom' says clearly that the town grew around the mines.
toegepas.fout: 'om die steenkoolmyne gegroei' is terse and a Grade 5 reader may stumble on 'om' before seeing it means 'around'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'rondom' says the same spatial relation (grew around the mines) more clearly; protected words stay intact.

laat_vaar.na: So groei 'n klein nedersetting uit tot
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Uitgroei tot' is the natural Afrikaans for growing into something bigger; the protected 'soms selfs tot 'n stad' stays intact.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'groei tot 'n dorp' is standard natural Afrikaans; 'uitgroei tot' is a lateral move in a sentence carrying the protected 'soms selfs tot 'n stad'.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Uitgegroei tot' is the idiomatic form, matching the previous block.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'het vinnig tot 'n groot stad gegroei' already reads well; the proposal is only different, and change 2 was not kept so there is no matching to restore.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Versprei lê' is awkward; settlements 'are spread' over an area ('versprei is').
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'versprei lê' is a natural Afrikaans form (lê versprei) and this is a glossary definition shared across lessons, so a lateral rewording must not be made here.

vlae.teks: Daarna kom huise, winkels, skole en ander dienste in die nuwe nedersetting by.
vlae.rede: 'En ander dienste' groups houses with services, which they are not; fixing it needs a content choice (for example dropping 'ander' or naming houses separately), so it is flagged rather than changed.

beskerm_bedenkings.rede: One entry protects 'Emalahleni' as a video word while the 'eMalahleni (Witbank)' entry lists 'Emalahleni' under NIE; the lesson correctly uses 'eMalahleni', but a case-insensitive guard may read the two entries as conflicting.
